title.narrative: Provision of integrated lifesaving WASH and Health services to conflict affected population in Xudun district of Sool region

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtAccording to joint inter-sectoral assessment conducted by several humanitarian partners, the displacement of Laascaanood in Sool region has adversely affected the population in all spheres of their live including the Water, Sanitation and Hygiene. As of today, over 185,000 people in Laas Caanood district have displaced as a result of ongoing armed conflict. Those affected include women, elderly, children. Severe water shortages have been reported across all the locations hosting the newly displaced people exacerbating the situation by putting pressure on the scarce resources available such as water points. Also, access to basic health services is very limitedlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtNODO is proposing 6-month integrated WASH and Health project targeting the most drought affected populations in Xudun district reaching a total of 18000 persons including (2,000 men, 9,000 women, 3,500 girls, and 3,500 boys). In this project, NODO is aimed to improve access to life-saving WASH and Health services for Xudun IDPs, Vulnerable host communities with recognition of people of disabilities, and the most vulnerable population through: -ltbrgt ltbrgt lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltbgtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtWASHlt/spangtlt/bgtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gt1) Provision of safe water drinking with water trucking for 50 days period. benefiting 9,000 i.e 1300 men, 7,000 women, 350 girls, and 350 boys) conflict affected IDPs and host communities will be under taken.ltbrgt 2) NODO organization will also construct 20 normal latrines to benefit residents in Xudun IDP sites which will also receive the clean water and hygiene promotions and hygiene kits, 3 additional latrines will be preserved for people living with disabilities who are living in the target locations.ltbrgt 3) 2500 Households will benefit from hygiene kit distribution and hygiene awareness. The hygiene kits will be procured locallyltbrgt 4) 10 Hygiene promoters will be recruited and trained lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gt5) Hygiene promotion campaign ltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family:"gttargeting 12,000 people lt/spangt
will be undertakenltbrgt6) Rehabilitation of 2 shallow wells ltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family:"gtbenefitting 2,000 people will be implemented.lt/spangtltbrgt7) 3 WASH committees will be established and trained to improve all preventive measures against the risks of AWD/cholera outbreaks in Xudun districtltbrgt8) Chlorination of the wells through recruited hygiene promoters i.e 10 shallow wells per week for the project periodltbrgt9) 80 sanitation tools will be procured and distributed ltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family:"gtas to improve the sanitation conditions in targeted IDP settlementslt/spangt
.ltbrgt ltspan style="font-family: helvetica, sans-serif text-align: left background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255)"gt10) Rehabilitation of 1 strategic boreholes with solar system and fully function water system in Xudun districtltbrgtlt/spangt11) Post-Distribution Monitoring to be done once during the project periodltbrgt ltbrgt ltbrgt lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal"gtltbgtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtHealth lt/spangtlt/bgtlt/pgt
ltpgtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtThe proposed project will support 2 static, 3 PHUs and 2 mobile centres in Xudun district. NODO plans to deliver an integrated package of promotive, preventive and curative maternal, new-born child health services and scale-up outbreak early warning and response and case management of epidemic prone diseases through response team as part of the efforts to support the drought affected communities in Xudun. The project aims to scale-up the static and mobile clinics in Xudun IDP and host community’s sites and scale up the health care through skilled health professionals. NODO through this project will provide regular medical supplies and life-saving drugs to established health facilities, establish referral mechanisms and improve the coverage of measles vaccinations, support safe motherhood and reproductive health while also ensuring readiness to prevent and respond to outbreaks such as malaria, measles or AWD/Cholera and promote health update through health education, beneficiary sensitization and management of GBVlt/spangtlt/pgt
